entries.en: How are you holding up, Lieutenant?
Not too bad. No headaches worth mentioning lately. Maybe I'm getting used to the strain.
Maybe you've just got a good stress release. I know that knocking the geth on their synthetic asses gets rid of my headaches.
Is it true that your biotic implants cause headaches, Lieutenant? I know some meditation exercises that might help.
Thanks, Liara. I'd appreciate that. Makes me wonder what it would have been like to have asari tutors instead of turians.
Given the attitude most young human males display toward my people, it seems turians were the best choice.
Your biotics are impressive, Lieutenant. I'm surprised that humans stopped using the L2 configuration with results like yours.
Is it true humans stopped using the biotic implants you were fitted with, Lieutenant?
You've got impressive biotic power. Humans should never have switched to the weaker L3 implants.
My headaches can be pretty bad, and I'm one of the lucky L2 implants. The L3's are safer.
Humanity will be judged by the sacrifices its people are willing to make, Lieutenant. The turians would have kept the L2 implants.
That makes sense. What use is harnessing that power if it causes more harm than good to your people?
You don't stop using a gun just because the kickback has a little sting.
Am I imagining things, LT, or are your abilities growing in strength?
Lieutenant? In the last few fights, your biotics seemed to pack more punch. Is it practice, or are you actually getting stronger?
Your biotic skill is extremely impressive, Lieutenant. I rarely see anyone with your level of ability.
Biotics are rare among quarians. I don't believe I've seen anyone except the asari with your strength, Lieutenant.
Your biotics are coming along nicely. In the last fight, it looked like you even surprised yourself.
I've always held back a little when I used my powers on living targets. Fear of hurting someone, I guess.
After what I saw on Eden Prime, I'm not holding back any more. Not against the geth, not against anyone.
So, Williams, are you happy you signed on with Commander Shepard?
I'm not sure, Lieutenant. Every time I think I have a handle on things, the universe banks hard to port.
Well, don't let anybody know. A big gun and a confident attitude will get you through a lot in life.
All this violence sometimes catches me by surprise. I imagine that your military training prepared you for it, Chief Williams.
Do you feel that your training in the human military prepared you well for your duties, Gunnery Chief?
My people are wanderers, not military leaders. All this fighting seems strange. It must be more familiar for you, Chief Williams.
This about normal for a human soldier's tour of duty, Williams?
Trying to take down a rogue Spectre and his army of synthetics? No, they didn't cover this in Basic.
Well, Garrus, any regrets about leaving Citadel Security?
So, Garrus, any regrets about leaving C-Sec?
Now that you have experienced a Spectre's life firsthand, Garrus, do you regret leaving your security position?
Do you ever regret leaving Citadel Security to pursue Saren, Garrus?
So, how about it, Garrus? Is this better than C-Sec?
Fighting a rogue Spectre with countless lives at stake and no regulations to get in the way? I'd say that beats C-Sec.
Well, we don't lack for excitement, that's for sure.
True enough. I'd rather be fighting than trust it to somebody else.
I am unsure how the imminent destruction of all organic life "beats" anything, but your enthusiasm is comforting nonetheless.
I'm pleased that the imminent destruction of all organic life has improved your career opportunities.
There may just be hope for you yet, turian.
Saren was one of the most respected turians in the galaxy, Garrus. Are you going to be okay going up against him?
Saren was one of the most respected turians in the galaxy, Garrus. Are you going to be okay going up against him?
Garrus, perhaps it is my own trouble with Benezia that makes me ask, but do you feel comfortable facing a respected turian Spectre like Saren?
Garrus--if you do not mind me asking--how do you feel about hunting a turian?
Must be hard for you, Garrus, knowing that the person behind all this death and destruction is a turian Spectre.
Saren is either a traitor or a madman. Taking him down will restore the good name of turians everywhere.
Just keep saying that, especially to humans. We've got a lot of angry people right now.
Just keep saying that, especially to humans. We've got a lot of angry people right now.
With your respect for the Spectres, I thought you might hesitate. I am glad I was wrong.
Things are different among my people. There are so few of us. We are expected to be loyal, even when it is difficult.
Glad to hear it. I was losing sleep over the prospect of people not loving the turians.
I'm surprised you're willing to fight krogan, Wrex. I thought you'd stand with your own.
I'm surprised you're willing to fight krogan, Wrex. I thought you'd stand with your own.
Considering the diminished numbers of the krogan, Wrex, I'm surprised that you are willing to fight and kill them.
I'm surprised that you're willing to kill your own, Wrex. Aren't the krogan just a few generations away from extinction?
You don't get it. For all your talk of honor and pride, the turians never had to test their principles in a real struggle.
How can you fight your own people, Wrex? There aren't that many of you left.
Anyone who fights us is either stupid or on Saren's payroll. Killing the latter is business. Killing the former is a favor to the universe.
So, Liara, you've spent fifty years studying Prothean ruins and artifacts?
So, Liara, you've spent fifty years studying Prothean ruins and artifacts?
With all this exploration of Prothean culture, this must be like a survey for you, Liara.
With all this exploration of Prothean culture, this must be like a survey for you, Liara.
So you've spent your entire adult life just studying old Prothean junk?
Our travels now are somewhat different from my normal excavations. I would prefer lengthier studies... and fewer explosions.
I think you've spoken for scientists everywhere, Liara.
I think you've spoken for scientists everywhere, Liara.
The loss of all this Prothean technology is just one more thing Saren will have to pay for.
Yes. Most of the technology I had hoped to bring back to the flotilla has subsequently attempted to kill us.
It's good for you. A nice explosion every now and then keeps the mind sharp.
I've heard some humans are angry at the quarians after the attack on Eden Prime. After all, you created the geth.
I've heard some humans are angry at the quarians after the attack on Eden Prime. After all, you created the geth.
Tali, are the quarians concerned that the return of the geth will lead to more anger against your people?
The geth killed billions and forced us from our homeworld. Most quarians believe we have paid properly for our mistake.
Hopefully having you with us fighting Saren will change people's minds.
Hopefully having you with us fighting Saren will change people's minds.
I hope the other races view matters in the same light.
The quarians endangered the entire galaxy when they let the geth break free. I hope your people are properly contrite, Tali.
As the turians are properly contrite for releasing the genophage upon the krogan?
You're assuming that sterilizing them was a mistake.
You quarians messed up the whole galaxy when you let the geth break free. Do your people ever talk about it?
Do the krogan talk about starting a foolish war that resulted in the turians sterilizing your people?
All the time.
Tali, why do you quarians wear those suits all the time? Is it a cultural thing?
Hey Tali, I heard a rumor that under those environmental suits, you quarians are partially synthetic.
I am curious about the helmet you always wear, Tali. Does it contain technical augmentation systems?
Your choice in armor is awfully limited, Tali. Couldn't you wear something without a helmet?
What's with the helmets, Tali? Are all quarians shy, or do you not believe in letting outsiders see your faces?
No. Living in the clean environment of the flotilla has weakened our immune systems. The environmental suits protect against diseases.
Oh. Well, I'll try not to sneeze.
It still makes you look a little like a geth, though. I'm just saying.
I suppose that makes it more likely you will return from your Pilgrimage, then. You are only truly safe on your flotilla.
So your people are forever wandering, and now they couldn't settle if they wanted to. I'm sorry.
Naturally. Anything that isn't constantly challenged grows weak.
Those asari commandos are impressive. Lightly armored, but their speed more than makes up for it.
Unless that speed lets them outrun bullets, I'm more inclined to stick with nice solid armor and a big gun.
Point taken.
Is it common for human women to be front-rank fighters, Chief Williams? I know that salarian women do not serve in the military.
I'm surprised to see you on the front lines, Chief Williams. Most women I've observed in your Alliance military serve in support roles.
Is it common for human women to be front-rank fighters, Chief Williams? I know that salarian women do not serve in the military.
It's becoming more common, but it took a long time to prove that "ladies" could handle an assault rifle or a shotgun.
I doubt anyone who saw your skill under fire could remain skeptical.
On the flotilla, we don't have the luxury of sexism. We need the best hands for every available job.
Sounds nice, but I don't think I could get used to the uniform.
Such enforced roles are common in dual-sexed societies. I was fortunate not to have to deal with that particular burden.
You handle yourself well, Williams. It's surprising. Krogan women have to stay home to try to reproduce.
Sorry to disappoint, Wrex. I'm not the stay-at-home kind.
Didn't say I was disappointed. I could get used to killing with women around. Gives the fight a different flavor.
I haven't spent much time with krogan before, Wrex. I have to say, you're not what I expected.
I haven't spent much time with any krogan before you, Wrex. I have to say, you're not what I expected.
Right. Because you humans have a wide range of cultures and attitudes, but krogan all think and act exactly alike.
Whoa! I didn't mean... look, just forget I said anything!
Look, I didn't mean--- Just forget I said anything.
Done.
You are unlike the other krogan I have met, Wrex. Your do not share the bloodlust of your people.
I'd been raised to see krogan as bloodthirsty thugs, but you've surprised me, Wrex. You are different.
The genophage is a lot easier to swallow when all krogan are savage monsters, isn't it?
Why don't you head back to the Normandy, kid? If you stay here in the real world, you might have to learn something.
Wrex, forgive the impertinence, but you are not like the krogan described in the stories on the flotilla.
When you're young, you go looking for every fight you can. You get older, you realize that the best fights will find you.
Liara, if your people don't need implants to use biotics, how come asari don't use biotics more often?
So, Doctor T'Soni, are all asari biotics? I heard Lieutenant Alenko say something about you not needing implants.
Sometimes I envy your biotic abilities, Doctor. But then, all your people have such skill.
Your biotic skill is extremely impressive, Doctor T'soni. Is that typical among asari?
Your biotics are pretty powerful. Are all asari that strong?
While the asari have natural biotic abilities, not all have the desire nor the skill to use their abilities effectively.
Are you kidding? To have that ability, without implants, and choose not to learn? I'll never understand the asari.
To have so many potential biotics that people can choose not to train... I imagine the lieutenant would be jealous.
Of course. I intended no disrespect to the effort you have put into your training. Pardon me.
And the asari are the most advanced race on the Council. I wonder if all Citadel races will eventually be natural biotics.
All that power, and some asari don't use it? You could've conquered the galaxy if you'd wanted to.
Evidently, we do not want to.
Hearing about the Protheans makes me wonder if some distant civilization is going to find our artifacts someday and study us.
No, sir. When some distant civilization finds our artifacts, we'll be right there to explain what they are.
I hope so, Williams, but I'll bet the Protheans thought the same thing.
I have often wondered the same thing, Lieutenant. Artifacts of vanished cultures are reminders of our own mortality.
All empires fall, Lieutenant. We can only hope that what we leave behind inspires respect and admiration.
The worlds we abandoned when the geth revolted serve as just such an example. It is a reminder of our mortality.
Feeling mortal, Alenko?
I'm not afraid to die. I guess I just want to be remembered by more than a few trinkets in a ruin somewhere.
It's strange. The geth are attacking, and everyone around here is still worried about ordinary business.
It's politics, Williams. The Council won't raise the alarm until they're certain about the threat.
The threat? Did they not see the vids of Eden Prime? See, this is why I hate politics.
I find it comforting. The pain and joy of ordinary life... that is what we are fighting to protect.
You're military, Chief Williams. They're civilians. Civilians never believe the enemy is coming until they're at the gates.
It's necessary, Chief Williams. Even if it comes to a full-scale war, someone has to provide food to eat and a home to return to.
Let them stay ignorant. If our mission reaches the point where these people need to worry about the geth, we've already lost.
Are you okay, Tali? It looked like you got some dirty looks back there.
Are you okay, Tali? It looked like you got some dirty looks back there.
I could not help but notice that you are attracting some unfriendly stares, Tali.
You seem to be attracting unwanted attention, Tali. Several passersby were staring at you.
Some people back there didn't like you, Tali.
Many think less of quarians for traveling in the flotilla, and for creating the geth. They see us as scavengers, little better than thieves.
Forget them. Anyone that ignorant isn't worth listening to, anyway.
That is sort of what I'd heard about your people. I guess you're not in any one place long enough for people to get to know you.
That is an ignorant opinion. Quarian explorers have uncovered more mass relays than any other race!
I am glad that some still remember the contributions my people have made.
It is natural for people to dislike rootless wanderers. If quarians would just settle another homeworld, you would not run into such concerns.
Perspective is a wonderful thing. Wait until their homeworld gets wiped out.
I'd love to see what the Normandy can do in a fight.
The Normandy isn't built for a stand-up fight. I'd rather rely on the IES than the shields.
The Normandy isn't built for a stand-up fight. I'd rather rely on the IES than the shields.
How so? The Normandy is built for stealth, not combat.
How so? The Normandy is built for stealth, not combat.
Only an idiot hopes for combat while flying in a stealth ship.
But the stealth drive adds a new tactical level to space combat as we know it. Surprise attacks, undetected flanking maneuvers...
I don't know, Garrus. I'd rather not be the first one up the ladder in terms of figuring out new tactics.
I don't know, Garrus. I'd rather not be the first one up the ladder when it comes to new tactics.
I had forgotten the turian appreciation for tactics and strategy. With respect, I hope we avoid ship-to-ship combat entirely.
If it comes to a fight, I'd prefer a flotilla ship. It's easier to trust what you've worked on yourself.
This isn't a strategy simulation. If those new tactics don't work, we're salvage.
So tell me, who'd win in a fight between you and Shepard?
What? Commander Shepard is my superior officer. I can't imagine us ever having to fight.
What? Commander Shepard is my superior officer. I can't imagine us ever having to fight.
You can't? That's why Shepard's your superior officer. And that's why Shepard would win.
Do krogan size up everyone for a fight, even friends and allies?
Do krogan size up everyone for a fight, even friends and allies?
Yes.
That question smacks of impertinence. Commander Shepard is a Spectre with a distinguished service record.
So was Saren. Think about it.
It must be nice to be back in civilization after so long in those Prothean ruins.
It must be nice to be back in civilization after so long in those Prothean ruins.
You must welcome civilization after spending such a long time in the Prothean ruins.
You must welcome civilization after so long a time in the Prothean ruins.
Being in the city must feel good after digging through rocks at that Prothean ruin.
No. Cities and stations were always my mother's area of comfort. I actually enjoy the solitude of dig sites.
When this is all over, you'll be able to go back to your rocks and ruins for as long as you'd like.
I don't think I could handle that. Eden Prime was as quiet and rustic as I'd ever want.
After seeing so many asari come through the Citadel, I assumed your people preferred large cities. I apologize.
The ship I grew up on was always full of noise and people. The solitude of a dig site would drive me crazy.
I'm surprised. I've never met an asari who didn't prefer clean clothes and a hot bath.
In other news, ExoGeni Corp is still denying reports that one of their survey teams has gone missing in the Hades Gamma cluster.
In breaking news, Chairman Burns of the Parliament Subcommittee on Transhuman Studies has been kidnapped by biotic extremists.
Presidium technicians are struggling to understand why a computer system catastrophically overloaded recently.
Alliance officials report that a geth incursion into the Armstrong Cluster has been repulsed, with the geth suffering heavy casualties.
A research facility in the Hades Gamma cluster was the victim of an attack by biotic extremists.
Miners in the Skyllian Verge are planning to resume operations on an asteroid rich in element zero.
A research station on Noveria has reportedly been destroyed. The exact cause is currently unknown.
A salarian excavation team has run into an unexpected problem after unearthing a Prothean dig site.
In entertainment news, Francis Kitt has announced plans to direct "Hamlet" with elcor cast members.
Treaty negotiations between the Alliance and the salarian republic have finally concluded.
When asked why communication with the survey team was suddenly cut off last week, company officials refused to comment.
ExoGeni Corp recently released an official statement regarding their missing survey team in the Hades Gamma cluster.
According to the statement, the remains of the survey team were discovered not far from their abandoned research camp. There were no survivors.
It is believed the researchers were the victims of a random attack by raiders or mercenaries. Names will be released after next of kin are notified.
C-Sec has declined to press charges in the death of human Conrad Verner, who was killed yesterday morning after assaulting a group of turians in a restaurant in the Wards.
Reporter Khalisah al-Jilani recently attempted to land an interview with Commander Shepard, the first human Spectre.
When pressed on the issues, however, Commander Shepard reportedly lost control and assaulted the reporter.
Commander Shepard answered difficult questions, demonstrating that under the military uniform is a keen diplomatic mind.
Terra Firma Party candidate Charles Saracino confirms that the first human Spectre endorsed his candidacy.
Admiral Kahoku, a respected member of the Alliance military, has passed away.
Because Verner initiated the assault, it has been ruled self-defense. Ambassador Udina has no plans to appeal the ruling.
Alliance officials have raided a dangerous cult controlled by a former Alliance officer, Major Kyle.
The biotics commandeered a freighter and were last seen in the Hades Gamma cluster. No demands have yet been made.
Technicians are reportedly unsure of what caused the malfunction, or even what the system was originally designed to do.
C-Sec is investigating the possible vandalism or misuse of public property.
In the event of future geth activity, the Alliance plans to maintain a strong security presence in the area.
Major Kyle and his cultists refused to surrender and were killed in the resulting firefight.
Major Kyle surrendered and is now being treated for severe post-traumatic stress disorder.
The veteran soldier, who won the love of his troops during conflict with the batarians, died of natural causes.
Kahoku is survived by his wife and three children, who are planning a small, private memorial service.
A daring Alliance raid killed the biotics. Miraculously, none of the researchers were harmed.
Drugged researchers were used as human shields, and there were several civilian casualties in the ensuing Alliance raid.
The facility is expected to re-open soon, with tighter security measures in place.
The drugged researchers attacked Alliance soldiers, and the rescue operation became a brutal massacre.
The research center is unlikely to re-open in the near future.
Raids by a criminal warlord had recently disrupted mining operations in the area.
After negotiations with the Alliance military, however, the warlord has allowed mining operations to resume.
The warlord was subsequently killed, however, and infighting among his lieutenants has made future raids unlikely.
Nonya Tombiri has been arrested and removed from her post as administrator of the Caleston mining station.
Administrator Nonya Tombiri of the Caleston mining station has vanished and is presumed dead following a violent incident at her offices.
Local officials have not provided details, but Tombiri was allegedly involved with the Caleston Cartel, a group of red sand dealers.
Administrator Tombiri's successor has not yet been named.
Administrator Tombiri of the Caleston mining station reports that the Caleston Cartel has been brought to justice.
The Cartel, a powerful group of red sand dealers, has defied authorities for years.
EAE, which owns the Caleston mining facility, was reportedly pleased that the Cartel is no longer operating in its station.
ExoGeni officials have announced that their research colony on Feros is being shut down.
Difficult living conditions combined with poor yield of viable discoveries made it unfeasible economically to keep the colony going.
After years of poor economic performance, ExoGeni has announced that its research colony on Feros is finally returning a profit.
New discoveries and a dedicated colonization effort have finally paid off for ExoGeni.
ExoGeni's stock rose sharply with the announcement, with investors pleased at this surprising news.
Given the research conducted on Noveria, many are blaming the destruction on an experiment gone awry.
Reports indicate that Administrator Anoleis died during the disaster. A new administrator has yet to be appointed.
Administrator Anoleis currently faces criminal charges as a result of the disaster, although the nature of the charges remains unclear.
Administrator Anoleis has released few details, except to say that investigations and repairs are ongoing.
Hanar protesters have blockaded the dig site, claiming that artifacts of "the Enkindlers", as the hanar call them, should not be disturbed.
The excavation team has appealed to hanar representatives on the Citadel to reach a diplomatic solution.
The production will open dramatic theater to the elcor with a Hamlet who uses elcor body language and pheromones.
Kitt claims that he is also excited by giving a human audience the chance to judge Hamlet by his deeds and not his emotions.
Binary Helix has settled out-of-court with a krogan group that had accused the genetics corporation of fraud.
The krogan group had contracted Binary Helix to perform studies with a long-range goal of curing their genetic sterilization.
The group later sued for a return of investment money when the study produced no viable results.
Salarian officials are complaining that the Alliance made unreasonable demands in hard-line negotiation tactics.
The resulting deal, negotiated by Elias Keeler, will bring billions of credits to the Alliance.
Salarians praised the openness and flexibility of Alliance negotiators in pursuing a deal that benefited both sides.
The deal was brokered by new Alliance negotiator Thomas Kent after his mentor Elias Keeler withdrew, citing health reasons.
Unfortunately, Shepard refused to answer questions, raising concerns regarding the Spectre's commitment to humanity.
We'll have exclusive footage later today.
Coming up in a report later today, Emily Wong investigates corruption on the Citadel and uncovers a full-blown crime syndicate.
Have increases in Citadel traffic endangered our safety? Emily Wong offers an inside look at the dangerous world of space-traffic control.
Later today, Emily Wong goes inside the fast-paced world of space-traffic controllers with an exclusive interview.
The Council isn't going to ask me any questions, are they?
I can't believe the Council ignored all the evidence against Saren!
Welcome to Port Hanshan, the galaxy's most respected site for independent scientific research and development.
In light of the recent attack on Eden Prime, many colonial investors are pulling their support for future projects.
In remembrance of Eden Prime, we present another profile in courage with Serviceman Nirali Bhatia.
Reports are circulating that Alliance Ambassador Udina has accused a Spectre of orchestrating the attack on Eden Prime.
In a further developments in the Eden Prime investigation, the Council has reportedly revoked the Spectre status of one of its operatives.
Celebrations are being planned for the anniversary of the end of the Rachni Wars.
Many Council worlds, particularly asari and salarian colonies, will hold victory parades to commemorate the defeat of the invading rachni.
In a rare admission of debt, several asari colonies have invited krogan to be honored for the victories the uplifted krogan made possible.
A devoted wife and talented chef, Serviceman Bhatia joined the Alliance military under the deferred education plan.
After finishing her service, Bhatia planned to open a restaurant. Instead, she gave her life protecting the colonists of Eden Prime.
For more profiles in courage, or to explore opportunities in the military, please visit the Alliance military on the extranet, keyword "courage".
Udina reportedly based his accusation upon eyewitness accounts of the scene, but lacked the evidence to demand further investigation.
When asked to comment, a Council spokesperson would only state that the investigation of the attacks upon Eden Prime was currently ongoing.
While the unnamed operative has not yet been apprehended, a Council spokesman confirmed that corrective actions had been taken.
I doubt it. We've made our reports. Now we just have to trust Ambassador Udina.
No we don't, sir.
Saren's one of their best operatives. It's only natural that they'd take his word over ours.
Oh, so now we just chase leads while this smug turian runs around with his geth troopers.
That's politics, Chief.
I hate politics.
I'm going to enjoy the look on the Council's face when they see evidence they can't just ignore.
I just hope it isn't too late. All this time we spent hunting for evidence gave Saren a nice head start.
There's no way the Council can ignore us this time. Saren's days as a Spectre are done.
If they had listened to me earlier, Saren would already be in custody. Every life lost because of that delay is on the Council's head.
There's no way the Council can ignore us this time. Saren's days as a Spectre are done.
Don't congratulate yourself too much. All this time you were hunting for evidence, Saren was moving forward with his plan.
If the evidence is worth trying to kill me for, I hope it is sufficient to motivate the Council.
You know, Saren would already be in custody if you'd gone straight to the Council with your information.
A lone quarian with no credentials? The  Council would laugh me out of the chambers. That is, if Saren hadn't killed me by then.
Watch yourself out there. Fai Dan said we wouldn't have any cover.
I imagine I've been in as many trench fights as you have, Lieutenant... if not more.
Keep your head down out there. Fai Dan said we wouldn't have any cover.
I shall endeavor to follow your lead.
Are you certain that this is the proper path? Fai Dan said we would not have cover from the geth.
Commander Shepard is choosing the best option. We can take the geth. The tunnels are an unknown quantity.
Multiple opponents and no cover makes for a difficult fight. Be careful out there.
At least the geth are a known quantity. Who knows what the beasts in the tunnels are like?
This is going to be bad, isn't it? Fai Dan said there was no cover out there.
I'll take a tough fight over tunnels. In a tunnel, they always know where you are.
For your own safety, and to protect the privacy of others, you are required to obey any directions given by our security personnel.
If you have questions or concerns, our friendly administrative staff is always available. Thank you, and enjoy your stay.
I have studied the Protheans for decades, but I have never felt this sense of foreboding. What will we find down there?
Whatever we find, be cautious. If this were simply an automated trap, Saren would have triggered it as well.
If this were simply an automated trap, Saren would have triggered it. What do you think this is?
Whatever it is, we should be careful.
What do you think we're going to find down here? It has to be useful, if it specifically targeted us.
I don't know. I just hope that whatever's down here is friendly. We've got enough enemies at the moment.
Whatever's down here is Prothean, right? So it has to be on our side, against the Reapers.
I'm not putting faith in anybody being on our side. Not any more.
What the hell is down here? Is this just another trap, or did we finally run into some good luck?
Don't get your hopes up. The only thing we can depend on right now is ourselves.
Proponents of expanded human colonization insist that Eden Prime was an isolated case. Nevertheless, colonist enrollment has dropped sharply.
Many colonial proposals are on hold until backers have some reassurance that human colonies will be adequately protected.
All their culture, all their advanced technology, and the Protheans were taken in by the Reapers, just as we were. They failed.
Just like my people. But they also gave us a chance to save ourselves. We must hurry!
It's tragic. For all their great achievements, the Protheans lost everything, just like my people. Even their last plan failed.
The Protheans did not fail. They gave us a chance. It falls to us to make the most of it, so I suggest we hurry.
So many races look up to the Protheans as paragons of civilization. But they were fooled by the Reapers, just as we were. They failed.
Not entirely. They've given us a weapon. They've given us a chance... if we can just get there in time.
So many dead for a plan that accomplished nothing. Saren gets through the Conduit, the Reapers arrive, and the Protheans fail.
We can get there in time. Their plan only fails if we do, and I've come too far to watch Saren win.
I can't believe it. So many dead, and it was all for nothing. The Protheans fell right into the Reapers' trap, just like we did.
Keep it moving. I've got no intention of ending up like them.
